h1: The 6 Best Under-Desk Printer Stands of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six under-desk printer stands and file cabinets from under $25 to $100, compared on height, storage, casters and ventilation.
summary: The HUANUO printer stand is the best under-desk option, topping out at 14.1 inches with a drawer, a rear cable channel and locking casters. The VASAGLE CUSTOS suits taller desks with two file drawers, and the Letaya adds three locking drawers. The HOOBRO is the choice for the tightest clearance.
intro: Under-desk printer stands fail on one measurement most buyers never take: the gap between the floor and the desk underside, with the printer's lid fully open. A stand that fits the printer but not the open lid means you drag it out every time you print, and a printer you cannot reach is a printer you stop using.

We reviewed six options that can hold a printer under a desk, from open shelves to file cabinets with a flat top. Ranking is based on the spec sheet: stand height, storage, casters, ventilation and price tier. We dropped a monitor riser that was designed for desktops, not floor use. The heights run from low shelves to 27.6 inch cabinets, so measure before you shop.

products.name: HUANUO Printer Stand with Cable Management and Storage Drawer
products.verdict: The most complete small stand, with drawer, cable channel and locking wheels.
products.description:
The HUANUO stands up to 14.1 inches high and has a rear cable channel, locking caster wheels and a drawer beneath the top shelf. It suits compact and mid-size printers. The caster locks matter most: without them, the stand creeps away when you pull the paper tray or slap a jammed sheet clear.

It beats the HOOBRO because of the drawer and lockable wheels, even though the HOOBRO sits lower. Both cost $25 to $50. It also costs a bracket less than the VASAGLE and Letaya cabinets, and it needs far less clearance than their 27.6 inch frames.

Buy it for a standard-height desk. The caveat is height and depth: at 14.1 inches it needs clearance for the printer plus an open lid, and the drawer is shallow, so it holds paper and cables rather than files.
products.idealFor: Standard desks with room for a mid-size printer.
products.skipIf: Your desk clearance is very low.

products.name: VASAGLE CUSTOS 2-Drawer File Cabinet Printer Stand
products.verdict: A real file cabinet sold as a printer stand.
products.description:
The VASAGLE CUSTOS measures 15.7 inches wide, 16.5 deep and 27.6 tall, with two drawers for A4 or letter documents, a matte black finish and a rolling base. It is sold as a printer stand, but it is really a small file cabinet with a flat top. That makes it a two-in-one for a corner desk.

It ranks under the HUANUO because 27.6 inches only suits taller desks, and it costs $50 to $100, a bracket more. But it replaces a separate file cabinet, which the HUANUO cannot do, and its rolling base lets you pull it out for toner changes. It also costs less than the Letaya.

Choose it if paperwork lives next to the printer. The caveat is security: the listing mentions no lock, so do not store sensitive files.

products.name: Letaya 3 Drawer Mobile File Cabinet with Lock
products.verdict: Three lockable drawers that roll under a desk.
products.description:
The Letaya has three lockable metal drawers, arrives fully assembled and takes letter, legal and A4 documents on a mobile base. Lockable drawers matter for tax papers, HR files or client documents, which are often what ends up near a home printer.

It ranks below the VASAGLE because it is not marketed as a printer stand, though the flat top works. It adds a lock that the VASAGLE lacks and a third drawer. Against the SISESOL, it offers one more drawer and wheels, but costs a bracket more at $50 to $100.

Ideal if you want private documents and a printer in one unit. The caveat is height and price: three drawers make it taller than most desks can accommodate, so measure carefully, and note that it is a filing cabinet first.
products.skipIf: You only need a printer platform.

products.name: SISESOL 2 Drawer File Cabinet with Lock, Narrow Vertical Filing Cabinet
products.verdict: A slim locking cabinet that fits narrow gaps.
products.description:
The SISESOL is a narrow vertical cabinet with two lockable drawers in black metal, listed for easy assembly and for letter, A4 and legal files. Its narrow profile slips into the gap beside desk legs, where a wider stand cannot fit.

It ranks under the Letaya because it has fewer drawers and no wheels in the listing, but it is cheaper in the $25 to $50 bucket and slimmer. Against the HUANUO it offers lockable storage, though it provides a smaller platform. Its black metal body is also sturdier than the open frames.

Good for a narrow gap beside the legs. The caveat is width: a narrow top limits printer size, so a wide all-in-one will overhang the edge and may be unstable.

products.name: HOOBRO 2-Tier Printer Stand with Charging Station
products.verdict: A low open two-tier shelf with a charging shelf.
products.description:
The HOOBRO is a two-tier open shelf with a built-in charging station shelf and a low, compact profile in a rustic brown and black finish. It suits compact printers. Low is the point: it fits under desks where the file cabinets and even the HUANUO would collide with the desk underside.

It ranks below the HUANUO because it has no drawer or casters listed, yet it fits tighter clearance. The open shelf gives easy access to a printer's paper tray and lid, and open air helps a warm printer. The charging shelf gives power for a phone or hub.

Buy it for a low desk. The caveat is that open shelves collect dust, and with no casters listed, you will lift or drag the stand to reach the back.

products.name: Hovadova Adjustable Mobile CPU Stand, Ventilated Computer Tower Stand
products.verdict: A cheap rolling frame that lets air through.
products.description:
The Hovadova began life as a tower stand, with a ventilated frame, four caster wheels and adjustable width. It costs under $25. The ventilated frame lets heat escape, which helps a laser printer that runs warm in an enclosed space.

It ranks last because it is not meant for printers and offers no storage. The adjustable width gives flexibility, but you must check the printer's footprint against the adjustable range, and the load rating is not stated. It does beat the cabinets on airflow and the HOOBRO on mobility, with four casters.

Buy it as a cheap rolling platform. The caveat is fit: confirm the printer's width and weight before ordering, since this frame was designed around PC towers.

whatMatters.detail: Measure from the floor to the desk underside, then subtract the stand height and the printer height with the lid open. Most failures happen on the lid. The HUANUO lists 14.1 inches maximum height, while the VASAGLE stands 27.6 inches. Check the listed height in the specs, and measure twice before you order, including the gap under any desk drawer or crossbar.

The top platform must fit the printer's feet with a little margin. A narrow top, like the SISESOL's, can leave a wide printer hanging over the edge. Compare the printer's width and depth to the stand's dimensions on the listing. Include the paper tray if it extends beyond the body, and check the weight the platform can carry.

Laser printers run hot and need airflow, so a fully enclosed cabinet traps heat. An open frame, like the HOOBRO or Hovadova, lets it escape. If you use a cabinet, leave the rear clear and avoid closing doors. Check the printer manual for ventilation clearance and operating temperature notes, especially for laser models.

Casters let you roll the stand out to load paper and clear jams. Locking wheels, like the HUANUO's, stop it moving when you pull a drawer or press the printer buttons. Look for locking in the listing, because wheels that cannot lock make a stand that wanders across the floor, especially on hard surfaces.

A printer needs power and often a data cable. A rear cable channel, like the HUANUO's, keeps them tidy and out of the way of the wheels. Without one, cables tangle around casters. Check the listing for cable management and consider where your power outlet sits, since a short cord limits where the stand can go.

faq.q: How do I measure for a stand?
faq.a: Measure from the floor to the desk underside, then subtract the stand height and the printer height with the lid open. If the number is negative, choose a lower stand like the HOOBRO, or raise the desk with risers.

Ignoring the open lid or paper tray. The printer fits, but you cannot use it without sliding it out. The 14.1 inch HUANUO needs clearance above it for the lid, so test the open height before you commit.

faq.q: Is a file cabinet stand worth it?
faq.a: If you keep papers near the printer, yes. The VASAGLE CUSTOS gives two drawers and a flat top. If you do not, a simple stand like the HUANUO is cheaper and needs less clearance under the desk.

faq.q: Can a laser printer sit in a cabinet?
faq.a: Leave the rear clear and avoid fully enclosing it, since heat builds up. An open frame like the Hovadova is safer than a closed cabinet such as the Letaya.

faq.q: How do I stop the stand rolling?
faq.a: Use locking casters, as on the HUANUO. Engage them after you roll the stand into place, and recheck them whenever you move it. Stands without lockable wheels may need a rubber stopper or wedge to stay put.

faq.q: Can I use a CPU stand for a printer?
faq.a: Yes, if the printer fits the platform width and weight limit. The Hovadova adjusts to fit tower sizes. Check the weight limit too, because the listing does not state the load rating.

finalTake: Buy the HUANUO if your desk has standard clearance and you want one compact stand with storage and locking wheels. Pick a file cabinet like the VASAGLE or Letaya only if the desk is tall enough and paperwork lives beside the printer. Measure with the lid open first, whichever you choose.
